extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners (inventors, patent attorneys/agents) filing with the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing patent drawings acceptable for USPTO publication and examination, addressing compliance with 37 CFR 1.84 and MPEP §608 standards (readability/reproducibility, disclosure support, offensive content, amendments, and design-practice requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings May Be Acceptable If Readable and Reproducible
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP 608.02(i): “Drawings that do not comply with all of the form requirements of 37 CFR 1.84 may be acceptable for the purposes of publication and examination if the drawings are readable and reproducible for publication purposes.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where formal requirements are not fully met, the USPTO may accept drawings provided they are clear enough to be read and reproduced for publication and examination. The page emphasizes practical flexibility but points to MPEP 608.02(i) as governing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted (as referenced in list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed as 'Permitted' in the related rules section (contextual tag in the FAQ list).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This tag in the page's rule-list indicates certain practices or departures may be allowed under MPEP guidance (see specific entries such as acceptability of non‑conforming drawings). No further detail given on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full and Clear Disclosure Required for Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP 608: A patent must contain a full and clear disclosure of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings must contribute to a full and clear disclosure—i.e., they should illustrate the invention sufficiently to satisfy the disclosure requirement. Page cites MPEP 608 as the governing manual section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for Full and Clear Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP 608 (listed again in the page’s rules): requirement that the application provide full and clear disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reiterates the necessity for drawings and text together to present the invention clearly. Page lists this as a distinct related rule (permitted/required tags vary on list).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Must Find Basis in Original Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP 608: Claims must be supported by and find basis in the original disclosure of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings cannot be used to add new claim-supporting matter after filing; they must support claims as filed. Page flags this as a required consideration under MPEP 608.

rubrics_metrics.name: No New Matter After Filing Date
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP 608: The application must not introduce new matter after the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment to drawings or text that would introduce subject matter not present in the original filing is impermissible. Page lists this as a related rule; consult MPEP 608 for particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original Disclosure Requirement for Filing
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP 608: The original disclosure at filing must meet statutory requirements (i.e., support and enablement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This underscores that drawings included at filing (and their content) form part of the original disclosure; they must therefore be adequate to support later claims and avoid new matter issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner Must Object to Offensive Language and Depictions in Patent Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP 608: Examiners should object to offensive language or depictions in applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings containing offensive or inappropriate depictions may be objected to by the examiner and should be corrected/resolved. Page marks this as recommended practice per MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and Drawings Must Be Resolved Before Publication
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP 608: Issues with language and drawings should be resolved prior to publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any objections (e.g., clarity, offensive content, non‑compliance) should be addressed so that the published application has acceptable drawings and text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for Design Application Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP 608: There are particular drawing requirements and practices that apply specifically to design patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design patents have specialized drawing standards (views, shading, broken lines, etc.); the page flags that design practice requirements exist under MPEP 608 and should be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and Other Papers Must Comply With Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP 608: Any amendments or other papers filed in the application must comply with applicable rules (including drawing/form requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting amended drawings or other documents, ensure they meet the USPTO rules or are at least readable/reproducible per MPEP 608.02(i); non‑complying submissions can be objected to or require correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Can Drawings Be Transferred Between Pending Applications?
rubrics_metrics.description: Related FAQ topic: whether drawings may be transferred from one pending application to another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists this as a related procedural question—transferability depends on practice and rules (see MPEP or USPTO practice guidance). No detailed answer is provided on the page itself, but it signals transfer/assignment of drawings is a relevant consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: What Makes Patent Drawings Acceptable for USPTO Publication and Examination?
rubrics_metrics.description: Related FAQ topic: criteria that make drawings acceptable for publication and examination by the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarized on the page by the key rule that drawings must be readable and reproducible for publication; formal compliance with 37 CFR 1.84 is expected but USPTO may accept non‑perfectly conforming drawings if they meet readability/reproducibility standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: How Does the USPTO Currently Classify Patent Drawings?
rubrics_metrics.description: Related FAQ topic: how the USPTO classifies patent drawings (classification topic listed on the page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists this as a related topic indicating classification matters (e.g., utility vs design, types of figures) are part of drawing practice; specifics are not provided on the page but are flagged as relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who Is Responsible for Pointing Out and Distinctly Claiming the Invention in a Patent Application?
rubrics_metrics.description: Related FAQ topic: responsibility for pointing out and distinctly claiming the invention (applicant’s duty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not limited to drawings, the page notes this related question because drawings may be used to point out and illustrate claimed features; ultimately the applicant (through the specification and claims) is responsible for distinctly claiming the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Can New Terms Be Introduced in Patent Claims After the Initial Filing?
rubrics_metrics.description: Related FAQ topic: whether new terms may be introduced into claims post‑filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ties back to the no‑new‑matter rule: introducing new terms that would add matter not supported in the original disclosure (including drawings) is impermissible. Page lists this as a related FAQ to drawing/disclosure rules.
